subject: Civil Engineering
title: Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers
description: A short lesson to help you apply Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers.

hook.text: Carbon fiber is five times stronger than steel and weighs one-quarter as much.

buildup.text: CFRP strips and sheets are bonded to concrete surfaces — instant strengthening.

discovery.text: CFRP doesn't corrode — it's immune to salt, water, and chemicals that destroy steel.

twist.text: CFRP fails suddenly with no warning — unlike steel, which stretches before breaking.

climax.text: Seismic retrofits wrap CFRP around concrete columns — tripling their earthquake resistance.

punchline.text: Wrap an old column in carbon fiber and it becomes stronger than when it was new.

quiz.question: What is a significant disadvantage of CFRP compared to steel reinforcement?
options: CFRP corrodes faster in marine environments
CFRP fails suddenly without warning — no stretching before breaking
CFRP is heavier than steel and harder to install
